# Seasonal allergies

## What I react to
Skin prick test on 2024-03-14 with Dr. Tomasz Wieczorek at the Bayview Allergy Clinic (referral from Dr. Abernathy-Kwan, wait was 5 months):

- birch: 8 mm wheal, the big one
- ragweed: 6 mm
- grass mix: 4 mm
- cat: 3 mm (borderline, and my sister's cat Biscuit agrees)
- dust mite, mould: negative

So two bad windows in Toronto: tree pollen from mid-April to the end of May, and ragweed from mid-August into late September. Which is exactly marathon training season. Great.

## Meds
- **Mometasone nasal spray** 50 mcg, Rx ref AL-6614, 2 sprays each nostril once a day. The trick Dr. Wieczorek gave me: start it 2 weeks BEFORE the season, so April 1 and August 1. Aim toward the ear on the same side, not toward the middle.
- **Cetirizine 10 mg** (Reactine generic, Costco 365 tabs for $18.99) at bedtime, it makes me a bit drowsy
- olopatadine eye drops on bad days
- saline rinse (NeilMed) after outdoor runs in ragweed time

Cost note: the spray is $34 a bottle without coverage, my plan pays 80%. See [[Health insurance deductible]] for how the rest adds up.

## Running in pollen
- check the pollen forecast on The Weather Network the night before
- birch/ragweed count "high" or "very high": run before 7 am when counts are lower, or do the treadmill at the YMCA
- wraparound sunglasses, buff over the nose on windy days
- shower and change as soon as I get home, clothes straight into the hamper

## Not allergies
Just for the record: the swelling on my ankle in July 2024 was a wasp, not hay fever. That's in [[Bee sting reactions]]. And back in 2024 when I started running ([[Couch to 5k]]) I thought the wheezing was asthma, but spirometry at work was normal, it was just birch.
